title: Containers and the Grid
summary: Bootstrap puts page content in containers. Its grid divides rows into 12 parts for arranging columns.
introduction: Bootstrap puts page content in containers. Its grid divides rows into 12 parts for arranging columns. Think of sharing 12 squares between boxes. Try two boxes with 6 parts each, then three boxes with 4 parts each.
learningObjectives: Choose between container, container-fluid and the breakpoint containers
Build rows of equal, fixed-width and content-sized columns
Adjust gutters, alignment and offsets with grid classes
Explain the padding and negative-margin mechanism behind row and col

blocks.text: A container is a centred block with horizontal padding that stops content stretching across very wide screens. `.container` has a `max-width` that steps up at each breakpoint; `.container-fluid` is always the full width of the viewport. Both add 12px of padding on the left and right, which is half of the default gutter and the reason columns line up with container edges, as you will see below.

`.container-md`, `.container-lg` and the other breakpoint containers are full width until the named breakpoint and then behave like `.container`. They suit pages that should fill a phone screen but not a monitor.

blocks.code:
.container: fixed max-width, centred

.container-fluid: always full width

blocks.title: Rendered result at a 1000px wide viewport
blocks.content:
First box: 960px wide, centred, with 20px of empty space on each side; the text starts 12px inside the border
Second box: 1000px wide, touching both viewport edges; the text starts 12px inside the border
The second box sits 1rem (16px) below the first because of mt-3

blocks.text: Inside a container you place a `.row`, and inside the row you place columns. The row is a flex container with `flex-wrap: wrap`, so columns sit side by side until they run out of room. Widths are expressed in twelfths: `.col-4` is one third of the row, `.col-6` one half, `.col-12` the whole row. Twelve was chosen because it divides evenly by 2, 3, 4 and 6, so most layouts need no fractions.

blocks.code:
Main content (col-8)
Sidebar (col-4)

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
One line with two bordered boxes: the first takes 66.67% of the row width, the second 33.33%
Each box has 1rem of inner padding from p-3
The left edge of the first box lines up with the container's left padding edge

blocks.text: Columns whose widths add up to more than twelve do not shrink; the column that no longer fits moves to a new line, because the row wraps. That is useful on purpose (a second line of cards) and confusing by accident.

blocks.text: You do not have to count. A bare `.col` has `flex: 1 0 0%`, so several of them share the row equally. `.col-auto` is only as wide as its content. `.row-cols-3` on the row makes every child one third wide without classes on the columns, which is ideal for lists of cards.

blocks.text: Columns are separated by **gutters**, and gutters are padding: every column has 12px of padding on each side, half of the 24px (`1.5rem`) gutter width stored in the `--bs-gutter-x` variable. To stop the first and last column being indented by 12px, the row has a negative margin of -12px on both sides. Padding and negative margin cancel at the edges, which is why column content aligns perfectly with the container's own padding edge.
The `g-*` classes set the gutter size from `g-0` (none) to `g-5` (3rem). `gx-*` changes only the horizontal gutter and `gy-*` only the vertical one, which matters when a row wraps onto several lines.

blocks.title: Rendered result
blocks.content:
Row 1: two bordered boxes whose borders touch in the middle; no space between them
Row 2: four boxes in a 2 by 2 arrangement with a 24px gap between the columns and a 24px gap between the two lines

blocks.text: Notice the inner `<div class="border">` in that example. Borders and backgrounds belong on an element *inside* the column, not on the column itself: the column's padding is the gutter, so a border on the column would wrap the gutter and the boxes would appear to touch.

blocks.title: Common mistake: skipping the row
blocks.text: Columns must be direct children of a `.row`, and rows should sit inside a container. Put a `.col-6` straight into a `.container` and its 12px padding adds to the container's 12px, so the content is indented by 24px and never lines up with anything. Put text straight into a `.row` and the row's negative margins push it 12px outside the container's edge. Whenever something is off by 12px, look for a missing row.

Because a row is a flex container, the [flexbox](/tutorials/css) alignment utilities work on it. `justify-content-center` centres columns that do not fill the row, `align-items-center` centres them vertically when one is taller, and `offset-*` pushes a column to the right by a number of twelfths using a left margin. `order-*` changes the visual order without touching the markup.

blocks.text: A column can contain its own row, and the twelve columns of that inner row span the width of the parent column, not the page. Nesting is how you build a sidebar with its own two-column widget list.

blocks.title: See the gutters
blocks.text: In the browser's DevTools, hover a `.col-*` element. The highlighted green padding area on each side is the gutter, and the orange margin area on the `.row` shows the matching negative margin. Resize the window and watch the container's max-width jump at 576, 768, 992, 1200 and 1400px.

questions.question: A row contains `col-6`, `col-6` and `col-4` in that order. Where does the `col-4` appear?
questions.explanation: The first two columns fill all twelve twelfths. The row wraps, so the third column starts a new line and is one third wide.
options: Squeezed onto the first line at a smaller width
On a second line, one third of the row wide
On a second line, full width

questions.question: To remove all space between columns you add the class `___` to the row.
questions.explanation: g-0 sets both the horizontal and vertical gutter to zero. gx-0 would remove only the horizontal one.

seo.description: Learn the Bootstrap 5.3 grid: container widths, rows and twelve columns, auto-layout, gutters, alignment, offsets and nesting, with the CSS behind each class.
